A_target.statement:
Let a finite group $G$ [[Definition:Group Action|act]] on a finite set $X$.
Then the number of [[Definition:Orbit (Group Theory)|orbits]] is:
:$\displaystyle \frac 1 {\order G} \sum_{g \mathop \in G} \card {\map {\operatorname {Fix} } g}$

B_source.statement:
Let $R \subseteq S \times T$ be a relation between finite sets.
Then counting the pairs of $R$ by first coordinate and by second coordinate gives the same total:
:$\displaystyle \sum_{s \mathop \in S} \card {\set {t: s \mathrel R t} } = \sum_{t \mathop \in T} \card {\set {s: s \mathrel R t} }$

substitutions.the relation R: the pairs (g, x) with g * x = x

derived.the two counts: the sum of fixed-point counts and the sum of stabilizer orders

object_map.reformulation: Double count the fixed pairs (g, x), then convert stabilizer sizes to orbit sizes.

validity_conditions: The orbit-stabilizer theorem is needed to rewrite stabilizer orders.
Finiteness of G and X makes all counts finite.
proof_plan: Let $F = \set {\tuple {g, x} \in G \times X: g * x = x}$.

By the source result:
:$\displaystyle \sum_{g \mathop \in G} \card {\map {\operatorname {Fix} } g} = \card F = \sum_{x \mathop \in X} \order {\Stab x}$
By the [[Orbit-Stabilizer Theorem]], $\order {\Stab x} = \dfrac {\order G} {\card {\Orb x} }$.
